research_rationale:
Executive Order 13581 of 2011-07-24 (76 FR 44757, PDF pages 1-3) is held as the Federal Register original (govinfo PDF text layer, grade official original). I read it in full and confirm its identity and its clause inventory of 23 scopes as prepared (a dup2 suffix distinguishes repeated item labels in different subsections). Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency with respect to significant transnational criminal organizations declared in Executive Order 13581 of July 24, 2011, under which additional steps were taken in Executive Order 13863. Notice of July 13, 2026 (91 FR 44727; FR Doc. 2026-14454) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond July 24, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain EO 13863 of March 15, 2019 (listed as a later event on the clause it amended) and annual continuation notices (July 21, 2025 and July 13, 2026), none of which is stated to revoke or supersede this order. The only later textual change found is Executive Order 13863 section 1, which rewrote section 3(e); it is recorded as a later event with before and after text on that clause. The dossier gaps listed as NOTICE identities absent from the census are annual continuation notices and cross-references, not events that change this order; the current-law pointer gaps concern CFR and Code pointers that this claim does not rely on, because the conclusion rests on the order's own text and the continuation notice. The acting-text lead for Executive Order 14294 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, May 9, 2025) was checked: a scan of the held corpus found no mention of this order in its text, so no provision targeting this order was located.
